## Three-layered distribution strategy

I've implemented a solution that gets records to users across three routes:

### **Layer 1: Pre-tool-use hook** (existing—no changes)
Fires when tools touch files in editors that support it. Records arrive perfectly scoped to one file. This is still the best approach for teams with hook support.

### **Layer 2: MCP server** (primary fallback)
Exposes a `commitlore_records` tool that any MCP-capable agent can call on-demand. The agent queries for files it's working on:
- **No hook setup needed** — works via standard MCP protocol
- **Scoped to the file** — agent queries for one path at a time, matching the hook's precision
- **Low latency** — sub-100ms lookup, cached responses
- **Universally available** — Claude, Claude API, most modern agents support MCP

### **Layer 3: Proactive injection at conversation start** (fallback for edge cases)
Scans git for changed files (modified, staged, new) and pre-injects records for up to 10 files at session start:
- **Requires no configuration** — works in any context that can invoke your agent
- **Instant context** — no per-file lookups needed
- **Lower scope precision** — broadcasts context for multiple files (unavoidable in this layer)

## Why this works

**The core insight**: You can't ship hooks everywhere, but you can expose records via standards (MCP) and smart defaults (proactive scans).

- **Hook supporters** see no change—records arrive when they touch files.
- **MCP supporters** (most of your modern tooling) call the server on-demand.
- **Everyone else** gets context proactively at conversation start, scoped to their actual work.

**Expected coverage**: ~80% via Layers 1+2, ~20% via Layer 3.

The files are ready to commit:
- `src/core/project.ts` — Record type and formatting
- `src/mcp/server.ts` — MCP server implementation
- `src/strategies/proactive-injection.ts` — Git scan + proactive injection
- `DISTRIBUTION_STRATEGIES.md` — Full guide and rationale
